system.name: DuVisor
system.one_liner: a delegated virtualization architecture that runs per-VM hypervisor processes in user mode via a hardware Delegated Virtualization Extension

components.name: VM
components.role: the guest virtual machine hosted by each hypervisor design

components.name: Hypervisor
components.role: monolithic hypervisor running entirely in kernel mode

components.name: Helper
components.role: user-mode helper process (or management VM) that hypervisor functions are offloaded to

components.name: Driver
components.role: kernel-mode driver retained in the host kernel after offloading functions to the Helper

components.name: DuVisor
components.role: per-VM hypervisor process running in user mode that handles the VM plane directly via DV-Ext

components.name: DV-driver
components.role: tiny kernel-mode driver remaining after the VM plane is offloaded to DuVisor

content.key_idea: Mainstream hypervisors progressively moved functions from kernel mode toward user mode (a to c), but this paper's delegated virtualization (d) goes further by running the whole VM plane in a user-mode DuVisor process enabled by a new hardware extension.
content.reading_order: Left to right across the four lettered panels (a) to (d), matching the historical progression named in the caption, with a legend at the top explaining arrow and fill meanings.

summary: This figure compares four hypervisor architectures to motivate DuVisor, a delegated virtualization design. Panel (a) shows a monolithic hypervisor running entirely in kernel mode; panel (b) shows mainstream hypervisors offloading general functions to a user-mode Helper process or management VM while a Driver remains in the kernel; panel (c) shows hardware virtualization extensions (like RISC-V H-Ext) adding H/V modes alongside U/K; and panel (d) shows this paper's delegated virtualization, where a user-mode DuVisor process handles the entire VM plane via a new hardware extension, leaving only a tiny DV-driver in the kernel. Blue dashed arrows marked 'Interact' and orange dashed arrows marked 'Offload' show how responsibilities move between modes, and gray/black/hatched fills distinguish general, VM-plane, hypervisor-plane and hardware-extension elements per the legend at the top.
summary_zh: 该图对比四种虚拟化架构演变：内核态单体 Hypervisor，卸载至用户态 Helper，引入硬件 H/V 模式，直至本文的委托虚拟化，将 VM 平面完全交给用户态 DuVisor。
notes: Panels (a)-(c) depict prior/mainstream hypervisor designs described only briefly in the introduction; exact internal box labels (e.g. 'Helper', 'Driver') are read from the figure itself since the surrounding text does not spell out every sub-box name.
